MCPToolProvider~emfModel.name: emf_model_tool_provider
MCPToolProvider~emfModel.description: Tools to author Ecore metamodels and to create, populate, validate and serialize EMF model instances (from allow-listed or session-registered EPackages)

MCPToolProvider~emfMetadata.name: emf_metadata_tool_provider
MCPToolProvider~emfMetadata.description: Discovery tools over the EMF metadata layer: locate a model by its EAnnotations, resolve a bare class name, and report what the metadata layer holds and how it is wired

MCPToolProvider~modelAtlas.name: model_atlas_tool_provider
MCPToolProvider~modelAtlas.description: Publishing tools handing a registered EPackage to the model atlas. Optional: this provider is absent unless org.eclipse.fennec.mcp.model.atlas.tools is deployed and a ModelAtlasPublisher is configured

MCPToolProvider~inference.name: inference_tool_provider
MCPToolProvider~inference.description: Task-scoped set for inferring a metamodel from sample payloads and handing it to the model atlas: discover the family and its conventions, author the package, validate it against the samples, register and publish. Deliberately omits instance manipulation, import/replay, operations and generics

HttpMCPServerComponent~inference.server.name: osgi-emf-inference-mcp-server
HttpMCPServerComponent~inference.server.instructions: Use this MCP server to infer an Ecore metamodel from sample payloads and hand it to this runtime's model atlas. DISCOVER FIRST: an unknown payload is usually a variant of a model that already exists, so start with list_annotation_sources (the annotation vocabularies of this runtime), then find_classes_by_annotation / find_features_by_annotation - OMIT 'value' to match any value for a key, which is how you locate a model family and check whether a discriminator value is still free. export_package emits the full .ecore of one registered package and is the only way to see its EAnnotations, abstract classes and supertypes as full <nsURI>#//<Name> references; describe_eclass and list_metamodel give the shorter view, describe_aspects reads one element's parsed provider metadata. AUTHOR: create_dataset, then create_epackage + add_eclass / add_eattribute / add_ereference / add_eannotation, with add_eenum(+add_eenum_literal) for a closed value set and modify_feature to correct a feature you already added. Type references are <nsURI>#//<Name> (e.g. http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore#//EString). Follow the conventions of the sibling models you found rather than inventing your own. VALIDATE: create_from_json builds an instance from one sample - load every sample and check nothing was silently dropped; export_dataset (format=xmi) serializes what you built. PUBLISH: register_package makes the package instantiable and is the precondition for post_to_model_atlas, which hands it to the atlas by nsURI - you never handle the document. Scope, stage and overwrite are fixed by the deployment; only allow-listed namespaces can be registered or published.

HttpMCPServerComponent~emfModel.server.name: osgi-emf-mcp-server
HttpMCPServerComponent~emfModel.server.instructions: Use this MCP server to author Ecore metamodels and to build EMF model instances. DISCOVERY (start here when you were handed a payload and not told which model it belongs to): list_annotation_sources reveals the annotation vocabularies of this runtime, so you never have to guess a source URI; find_classes_by_annotation/find_features_by_annotation/find_operations_by_annotation then query across every registered package at once - OMIT 'value' to match any value for a key, which is how you locate a whole model family and check whether a discriminator value is still free; find_class_by_name resolves a bare class name to its <nsURI>#//<Name> reference; describe_aspects reads one element's parsed provider metadata (and its diagnostics); list_aspects and describe_metadata_status report what the metadata layer holds and how it is wired. These reach every registered package, including ones no allow-list mentions, and return identities rather than model content. INSTANCES: start with list_metamodel and describe_eclass to discover the metamodel, then create_dataset + create_instance + modify_feature to build objects; inspect_dataset (includeRecipe=true) returns a replayable recipe; export_dataset serializes XMI or JSON; export_package emits the full .ecore of one registered package - the only way to see a model's EAnnotations, its abstract classes and its supertypes as full <nsURI>#//<Name> references, all of which describe_eclass omits; create_from_json builds a whole graph in one call; replay_recipe reproduces a dataset deterministically. AUTHORING: create_dataset then create_epackage + add_eclass/add_edatatype/add_eenum(+add_eenum_literal)/add_eattribute/add_ereference/add_eoperation(+add_eparameter)/add_eannotation, with add_etypeparameter and eGenericType/eGenericSuperTypes for generics; type references are <nsURI>#//<Name> (e.g. http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore#//EString) or a dataset objectId; register_package validates and registers the package so its classes become instantiable (list_registry/unregister_package manage it); export_dataset (format=xmi) yields the .ecore. IMPORT: import_ecore / import_instances re-load inline XMI to keep editing across prompts (import the .ecore before its instances). SECURITY: OSGi packages are visible only when allow-listed (deny-all); authored packages register only under allow-listed namespaces and must be dynamic; imported XMI is never dereferenced externally.
